question: Must a traveller pray four behind a resident imam, and may a travelling imam shorten the prayer?
answer:
The third point: a lot of times questions come about a musafir praying behind a muqim, a muqim praying behind a musafir, etc. I just want to do this quickly. Pretty much there is unanimous consensus in this regard: if a musafir is praying behind a muqim — you are traveling, you have the permissibility to pray two rak'ahs, but you come to a masjid, now the imam is not traveling and the imam prays four — pretty much, I would say there's one or two, but essentially, **by almost unanimous consent, you must pray four rak'ahs.**

Why? Because in the hadith, the imam has been made to be followed. Once you join the congregation, you are following the imam. And praying the full four is permissible; it's not haram for you. It's permissible, and following the imam is wajib, so we prefer the wajib over the permissible. Because praying two is Sunnah, praying four is ja'iz, it's permissible. If you were alone, it would be against the Sunnah, but now that you're in a jama'ah, you will pray all four.

And the opposite also applies, if the musafir is leading. As we all know — and this is reported from the Sahaba — some of them led the salah, and after two rak'ahs they finished, and they said, 'Inna qawmun 'ala safar' — we are a people who are traveling, so you continue your salah. So the imam prays two rak'ahs. And obviously everybody knows this: if you're not a musafir, you don't just get a concession because the imam is praying two rak'ahs. No, you have to pray the full four.

By the way, that having been said, even though it is allowed for the imam who's a musafir to pray two, some of our scholars have said that if there's a jama'ah, it would be better for him to pray four, to not cause confusion. Because these days people don't know fiqh and whatnot, and the imam prays two, and it's asr or maghrib — sorry, isha — like, 'What? What is going on?' It's ja'iz for the imam, and in this case the imam in his heart wants to follow the Sunnah, but for the sake of the congregation, not to make them confused...

And me personally, as a rule: if I'm leading three or four people, okay, they know, we can tell. But if I'm leading in a masjid — I'm invited everywhere — every time I lead in a masjid, I never do two rak'ahs. Because there's 200 people, 500 people, and just for my convenience, it's going to make them confused. And our scholars have said this: the imam has the option; now you should weigh the pros and cons. Nonetheless, if I were to do this, or anybody were to do this, it is ja'iz. The announcement can be made, and the imam will pray two, and the people behind will pray four rak'ahs.
